claims.claim: HTTP is a stateless application-level protocol whose shared semantics cover request-response communication.
HTTP is a client-server protocol for fetching resources, and a browser commonly initiates the request.
An HTTP message includes control data, header fields, and potentially content; request control data includes method and target, while response control data includes a status code.
GET requests transfer of a current selected representation of the target resource, while POST asks the target resource to process enclosed content according to its own semantics.
HTTP response status codes are three-digit integers from 100 through 599, with the first digit defining the response class.
The 204 status indicates successful fulfillment with no additional response content, and 404 Not Found is a 4xx client-error-class status.
